rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid reports the Prophet’s night journey from the Haram on al-Buraq, whose stride reached the horizon, to Jerusalem, where he tied it at the prophets’ ring.
rows.anchor: فبينا أنا نائم عشاء في المسجد الحرام، إذ أتاني آت فأيقظني، فاستيقظت فلم أر شيئا، وإذا أنا بكهيئة خيال،

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: The Prophet declines callers on his right and left; Gabriel identifies them as Jewish and Christian invitations and says accepting either would have led the community to that religion.
rows.anchor: قال: ذاك داعي اليهود، أما إنك لو أجبته -أو: وقفت عليه-لتهودت أمتك

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: An adorned woman with uncovered arms represents the world; Gabriel says accepting her would make the community prefer worldly life to the hereafter.
rows.anchor: قال: تلك الدنيا، أما إنك لو أجبتها أو أقمت عليها، لاختارت أمتك الدنيا على الآخرة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: In Jerusalem the Prophet is offered wine and milk, chooses milk, and Gabriel calls that choice the natural disposition (fiṭra).
rows.anchor: فأتاني (4) جبريل، عليه السلام بإناءين: أحدهما خمر، والآخر لبن، فشربت اللبن، وتركت الخمر، فقال جبريل: أصبت الفطرة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The Prophet and Gabriel pray two cycles in Jerusalem before ascending by a wondrous ladder through which human souls ascend; the report describes immense angelic hosts at the lowest heaven.
rows.anchor: ثم دخلت أنا وجبريل بيت المقدس، فصلى كل واحد منا ركعتين

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: At the lowest heaven, Ismāʿīl presides over seventy thousand angels, each with a hundred-thousand-angel host; the report quotes that only God knows His armies.
rows.anchor: وهو صاحب السماء الدنيا وبين يديه سبعون ألف ملك، مع كل ملك جنده مائة ألف ملك

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Adam sees the souls of his descendants: he calls believers’ souls pure and assigns them to ʿIlliyyūn, while wicked souls are impure and assigned to Sijjīn.
rows.anchor: هو تعرض عليه أرواح ذريته المؤمنين، فيقول: روح طيبة، ونفس طيبة، اجعلوها في عليين

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: People leave lawful food untouched and eat rotten forbidden meat; Gabriel identifies them as members of the Prophet’s community who abandon the lawful for the unlawful.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء من أمتك يتركون الحلال ويأتون (2) الحرام.

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Usurers appear with house-sized bellies, collapsing whenever they try to rise; the report identifies them with those who consume usury, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء من أمتك {الذين يأكلون الربا لا يقومون إلا كما يقوم الذي يتخبطه الشيطان من المس} [البقرة: 275] .

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: People with camel-like lips are force-fed burning coals that pass through them; Gabriel identifies them as unjust consumers of orphans’ property.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء من أمتك {الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلما إنما يأكلون في بطونهم نارا وسيصلون سعيرا} [النساء: 10] .

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Women hanging by their breasts are identified as adulterers from the Prophet’s community.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء الزناة من أمتك

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: People who cut flesh from their own sides and are told to eat it represent those who backbite and slander others.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء الهمازون من أمتك اللمازون

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The ascent report places Joseph in the second heaven, John and Jesus in the third, Idrīs in the fourth, Aaron in the fifth, Moses in the sixth, and Abraham in the seventh.
rows.anchor: ثم صعدت إلى السماء السابعة، فإذا أنا بأبينا إبراهيم (2) خليل الرحمن ساند ظهره إلى البيت المعمور

rows.speaker: موسى بن عمران
rows.claim: Moses says people assume he is most honored before God, but acknowledges that Muhammad is more honored than he is.
rows.anchor: يزعم الناس أني أكرم على الله من هذا، بل هذا أكرم على الله تعالى مني

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The Prophet finds his community divided between white and grey garments; the white-clothed enter the Frequented House, while the others are barred though still regarded as good, and seventy thousand angels pray there daily without returning.
rows.anchor: والبيت المعمور يصلى فيه كل يوم سبعون ألف ملك، لا (5) يعودون فيه إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: At the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, a spring called Salsabīl divides into the Kawthar and Mercy rivers; washing there is said to forgive the Prophet’s past and future sins.
rows.anchor: فإذا كل ورقة منها تكاد أن تغطي هذه الأمة، وإذا فيها عين تجري يقال لها: سلسبيل،

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A maiden says she belongs to Zayd ibn Ḥāritha; the Prophet sees Paradise’s rivers and fruit and repeats that God has prepared for the righteous what no eye has seen or heart imagined.
rows.anchor: فاستقبلتني جارية، فقلت: لمن أنت يا جارية؟ فقالت (6) لزيد بن حارثة، وإذا

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The Prophet describes Hell as God’s wrath and retribution, saying it would consume stones and iron, before it is closed from him.
rows.anchor: ثم عرضت علي النار، فإذا فيها غضب الله وزجره ونقمته، لو طرح فيها الحجارة والحديد لأكلتها،

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: At the Lote Tree the Prophet is brought near to God by two bow-lengths or less; angels descend on its leaves, and the wording recalls the Qurʾānic description.
rows.anchor: فتغشاني فكان بيني وبينه قاب قوسين أو أدنى

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Fifty prayers are prescribed, then Moses repeatedly urges relief until five remain; good intentions and deeds earn multiplied reward, so five prayers count as fifty.
rows.anchor: وفرضت علي خمسون (11) وقال: لك بكل حسنة عشر، إذا هممت بالحسنة فلم تعملها كتبت لك حسنة،

rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: When the five prayers remain, Moses urges another request for relief, but the Prophet says he has returned to God until he is ashamed to ask again.
rows.anchor: ثم رجعت إلى موسى فقال: بم أمرت؟ فقلت: بخمس صلوات. قال: ارجع إلى ربك فاسأله التخفيف،

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The next morning the Prophet reports visiting Jerusalem and ascending; after Abū Jahl mocks him, he describes a Quraysh caravan and Jerusalem’s structure, which a questioner confirms.
rows.anchor: فرفع لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيت المقدس من مقعده، فنظر إليه كنظر أحدنا إلى بيته:

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abū Jahl ridicules the claim that the Prophet reached Jerusalem in one night, contrasting it with the two-month caravan journey there and back.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو جهل -يعني ابن هشام-: ألا تعجبون مما يقول محمد؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr says Abū Hārūn al-ʿAbdī was judged weak by hadith critics, but includes his account because it contains corroborating details for other reports.
rows.anchor: وهو مضعف عند الأئمة (3)

rows.speaker: يزيد بن أبي حكيم
rows.claim: Yazīd reports a dream in which the Prophet affirms an Abū Saʿīd account but calls extravagant Israʾ stories the storytellers’ lore; in the dream he also says Sufyān al-Thawrī is reliable.
rows.anchor: فقال لي: "ذلك (10) حديث القصاص"

rows.speaker: شداد بن أوس
rows.claim: Shaddād’s account has Gabriel take the Prophet from Mecca to Medina, Madyan, Bethlehem, and Jerusalem, where he ties the mount and prays with the angels.
rows.anchor: شداد بن أوس قال: قلنا: يا رسول الله، كيف أسري بك؟ قال:

rows.speaker: شداد بن أوس
rows.claim: Offered milk and honey in Jerusalem, the Prophet chooses milk; a present elder says he has chosen the natural disposition and is rightly guided.
rows.anchor: فأخذت اللبن فشربت (2) حتى قرعت به جبيني، وبين يدي شيخ متكئ على مثواة له، فقال: أخذ صاحبك الفطرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says the view of Hell was like a hot bath; he then reports passing a Quraysh caravan and predicting its arrival and lead camel, which later matches.
rows.anchor: قال: مثل الحمة السخنة. ثم انصرف بي (4) فمررنا بعير لقريش بمكان كذا وكذا،

rows.speaker: شداد بن أوس
rows.claim: When Abū Bakr asks for a description of Jerusalem, the Prophet says the city is made visible to him and he answers each question about it.
rows.anchor: ففتح لي صراط كأني أنظر إليه لا يسألني عن شيء إلا أنبأته عنه

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqī calls the Shaddād report’s chain sound; Ibn Kathīr says it mixes sound material with objectionable details, especially prayer at Bethlehem and Abū Bakr asking for Jerusalem’s description.
rows.anchor: هذا إسناد صحيح، وروى ذلك مفرقا في أحاديث غيره، ونحن نذكر من ذلك إن شاء الله ما حضرنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet hearing Bilāl’s footsteps in Paradise and seeing Moses, Jesus, and Abraham; in Hell, people eating carrion are identified as those who consume others’ flesh.
rows.anchor: ليلة أسري بنبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم دخل الجنة، فسمع في جانبها وجسا (9)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: At Jerusalem all the prophets pray with the Prophet; he then chooses milk over honey, and the attendant declares that he has chosen the natural disposition.
rows.anchor: فإذا النبيون أجمعون يصلون معه. فلما انصرف جيء بقدحين، أحدهما عن اليمين والآخر عن الشمال،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The same account identifies a conspicuously red-blue man as the killer of the she-camel and says the Prophet saw him during the night journey.
rows.anchor: ورأى رجلا أحمر أزرق جدا،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One Ibn ʿAbbās route says some listeners rejected the Prophet’s account and became unbelievers; Abū Jahl mocks the warning of Zaqqum by eating dates and butter.
rows.anchor: فارتدوا كفارا، فضرب الله رقابهم مع أبي جهل (3) وقال أبو جهل (4) يخوفنا محمد بشجرة الزقوم،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet says he saw the Dajjāl awake, and gives descriptions of the Dajjāl, Jesus, Moses, Abraham, and Mālik, Hell’s keeper; al-Nasāʾī’s route is graded sound.
rows.anchor: ورواه النسائي من حديث أبي زيد ثابت بن يزيد (5) عن هلال -وهو ابن خباب- به، وهو (6) إسناد صحيح.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A further report describes Moses as tall and curly-haired and Jesus as medium-built, reddish-white, and straight-haired; Qatāda interprets the verse as the Prophet’s meeting Moses.
rows.anchor: فكان قتادة يفسرها: أن نبي الله [صلى الله عليه وسلم] (7) قد لقي موسى [عليه السلام] (8)

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda also explains the statement that Moses was made guidance for the Children of Israel as meaning God made Moses their guide.
rows.anchor: {وجعلناه هدى لبني إسرائيل} قال: جعل الله موسى هدى لبني إسرائيل (9)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report links a sweet scent on the journey to Pharaoh’s believing hairdresser and her children, who were thrown into heated copper; an infant tells its mother to stand firm in truth.
rows.anchor: "لما أسري بي، مرت بي رائحة طيبة، فقلت: ما هذه الرائحة؟ قالوا: ماشطة بنت فرعون وأولادها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr calls this chain acceptable and notes four infants who spoke: the hairdresser’s child, Joseph’s witness, the companion of Jurayj, and Jesus.
rows.anchor: إسناد لا بأس به، ولم يخرجوه.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After the journey the Prophet fears people will disbelieve him; Abū Jahl draws the crowd out, asks for Jerusalem’s description, and the city is shown to the Prophet so he can describe it accurately.
rows.anchor: فجيء بالمسجد وأنا أنظر إليه، حتى وضع دون دار عقيل -أو عقال- فنعته وأنا أنظر إليه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the Lote Tree is in the sixth heaven, the limits for what ascends and descends; it is veiled by golden moths, and the Prophet receives five prayers, the closing verses of al-Baqara, and forgiveness for major sins absent shirk.
rows.anchor: فانتهى إلى سدرة المنتهى، وهي في السماء السادسة، وإليها ينتهي ما يصعد به حتى يقبض منها،

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqī calls Ibn Masʿūd’s report one portion of the Ascension account and notes versions from Anas through Mālik ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa, from Abū Dharr, and in mursal form.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره عبد الله بن مسعود طرف من حديث المعراج، وقد رواه أنس بن مالك، عن مالك بن صعصعة،

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A rare Ibn Masʿūd report describes Gabriel’s mount and meetings with Moses and Abraham; Abraham urges the Prophet to prioritize intercession for his weak, last community.
rows.anchor: قال: هذا أحمد (11) ، قال: مرحبا بالنبي الأمي العربي، الذي بلغ رسالة ربه، ونصح لأمته

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة بن عبد الله
rows.claim: At Jerusalem the Prophet recognizes the prophets, drinks milk from the offered milk and honey, then leads the prophets in prayer.
rows.anchor: ثم دخلت المسجد فعرفت النبيين من بين راكع وقائم وساجد

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Gabriel says Moses rebukes God on the Prophet’s behalf and raises his voice, but God knows Moses’ temper.
rows.anchor: إن الله [عز وجل] (1) قد عرف له حدته

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: A report says Abraham, Moses, and Jesus discuss the Hour but none knows its timing; Jesus says the Dajjāl will emerge and he will destroy him, after which Gog and Magog devastate the lands until God destroys them and the Hour comes suddenly.
rows.anchor: لقيت ليلة أسري بي إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى، فتذاكروا أمر الساعة

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن قرط
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Qurṭ reports that Gabriel and Michael flew the Prophet from between Zamzam and the Station to the heavens, where he heard the heavens’ glorification.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة أسري به من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى كان بين زمزم (2) والمقام،

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: When Kaʿb advises praying behind the Rock so Jerusalem lies before him, ʿUmar rejects the Jewish-like orientation, prays where the Prophet prayed, and clears rubbish from the Rock.
rows.anchor: فقال عمر رضي الله عنه: ضاهيت اليهودية، [لا] (6) ولكن أصلي حيث صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr says ʿUmar neither treated the Rock as a qibla like Jews nor dishonored it as Christians had; he removed the litter, consistent with the ban on sitting or praying toward graves.
rows.anchor: وهذا شبيه بما جاء في صحيح مسلم عن أبي مرثد الغنوي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تجلسوا على القبور ولا تصلوا إليها"

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A very long and unusual report, with Abū Jaʿfar uncertain whether its authority is Abū Hurayra, says Gabriel washes and opens the Prophet’s heart with Zamzam and seals him with prophethood.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أو غيره -شك أبو جعفر-في قول الله عز وجل: {سبحان الذي أسرى بعبده ليلا من المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: In the vision, people who fight in God’s path harvest crops that regrow daily, receiving seven hundredfold reward and replacement for what they spend.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء المجاهدون في سبيل الله، تضاعف لهم الحسنة بسبعمائة ضعف، وما أنفقوا من شيء فهو يخلفه،

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: People whose heads are repeatedly crushed are those who neglect obligatory prayer; people failing to pay alms are punished with tormenting food.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء الذين تتثاقل رءوسهم عن الصلاة المكتوبة. ثم أتى على قوم على أقبالهم رقاع،

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Men and women who leave lawful spouses for unlawful partners represent adulterous betrayal of marriage.
rows.anchor: هذا الرجل من أمتك، تكون عنده المرأة الحلال الطيبة، فيأتي امرأة خبيثة فيبيت عندها حتى يصبح،

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: People who sit across a road and tear passing clothes represent those who block the path; the narration quotes the prohibition on sitting along every road to threaten and obstruct.
rows.anchor: هذا مثل أقوام من أمتك، يقعدون على الطريق يقطعونه (7) ثم تلا {ولا تقعدوا بكل صراط توعدون

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: A man carrying an unmanageable pile of wood and adding more represents someone burdened by others’ trusts that he cannot repay but still accepts more.
rows.anchor: هذا الرجل من أمتك يكون عليه أمانات الناس لا يقدر على أدائها وهو يريد أن يحمل عليها

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: Preachers whose tongues and lips are repeatedly cut with iron shears are identified as speakers who stir up strife.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء خطباء الفتنة

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: A huge bull that cannot return through its small hole represents a person who utters a grave word and then cannot take it back.
rows.anchor: هذا الرجل يتكلم بالكلمة العظيمة ثم يندم عليها فلا يستطيع أن يردها

rows.speaker: الجنة
rows.claim: Paradise asks God to fulfill its promise; God grants it to Muslims and believers who trust Him alone, do good, fear Him, ask Him, and rely on Him.
rows.anchor: لك كل مسلم ومسلمة، ومؤمن ومؤمنة، ومن آمن بي وبرسلي وعمل صالحا ولم يشرك بي، ولم يتخذ من دوني أندادا،

rows.speaker: جهنم
rows.claim: Hell likewise asks for its promised inhabitants; God assigns it polytheists, unbelievers, the wicked, and tyrants who deny the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: لك كل مشرك ومشركة، وكافر وكافرة، وكل خبيث وخبيثة، وكل جبار لا يؤمن بيوم الحساب.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: At Jerusalem the Prophet ties his mount to the Rock, prays with the angels, and is welcomed by them as their brother and successor.
rows.anchor: فنزل فربط فرسه إلى صخرة، ثم دخل فصلى مع الملائكة، فلما قضيت الصلاة قالوا: يا جبريل، من هذا معك؟

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Abraham praises God for making him a friend, granting kingship, making him a devout exemplar, and rescuing him from the Fire.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي اتخذني خليلا وأعطاني ملكا عظيما، وجعلني أمة قانتا يؤتم بي،

rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: Moses praises God for speaking to him, destroying Pharaoh’s people, saving Israel through him, and giving his community people who guide and judge justly.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي كلمني تكليما، وجعل هلاك آل فرعون ونجاة بني إسرائيل على يدي،

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: David praises God for kingship, the Psalms, softened iron, mountains and birds glorifying God, wisdom, and decisive speech.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي جعل لي ملكا عظيما، وعلمني الزبور، وألان لي الحديد،

rows.speaker: سليمان
rows.claim: Solomon praises God for subjecting winds, jinn, humans, and birds, teaching him their speech, granting him a unique righteous kingdom, and giving him abundance.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي سخر لي الرياح، وسخر لي الشياطين يعملون لي ما شئت من محاريب وتماثيل،

rows.speaker: عيسى
rows.claim: Jesus praises God for making him His word, teaching scripture, enabling miracles by permission, and protecting him and his mother from Satan.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي جعلني كلمته وجعل مثلي مثل آدم، خلقه من تراب ثم قال له: "كن" فيكون،

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: Muhammad praises God for sending him as mercy and universal herald, revealing the Criterion, making his community the best and a middle community, expanding his breast, lifting his mention, and making him opener and seal; Abraham says this favors him above them.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي أرسلني رحمة للعالمين، وكافة للناس بشيرا ونذيرا، وأنزل علي الفرقان

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الرازي
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī glosses Muhammad’s being the seal as the final prophet and the opener as his intercession on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: خاتم النبوة، فاتح بالشفاعة يوم القيامة.

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: The Prophet declines wine after drinking milk; Gabriel says wine will be forbidden to the community and that only a few would follow the Prophet had he drunk it.
rows.anchor: أما إنها ستحرم على أمتك، ولو شربت منها لم يتبعك من أمتك إلا قليل.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In the first heaven Adam is fully formed, joyful when descendants enter Paradise and sorrowful when they enter Hell; Jesus and John are encountered together in the second heaven.
rows.anchor: قال: هذا عيسى ابن مريم، ويحيى بن زكريا، ابنا الخالة عليهما السلام.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In the third heaven Joseph is described as more beautiful than other people, like the full moon among the stars.
rows.anchor: فإذا هو برجل قد فضل على الناس في الحسن كما فضل القمر ليلة البدر على سائر الكواكب،

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The report places Idrīs in the fourth heaven, beloved Aaron with the Children of Israel in the fifth, and Moses in the sixth; Moses grieves that Muhammad carries a larger community than he does.
rows.anchor: هذا هارون المحبب [في قومه] (3) وهؤلاء بنو إسرائيل. ثم صعد به إلى السماء السادسة فاستفتح،

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abraham sits at the seventh heaven; people with radiant faces are those whose faith was not mixed with wrongdoing, while repentant people emerge purified through three rivers.
rows.anchor: قوم لم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم. وأما هؤلاء الذين في ألوانهم شيء، فقوم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا، فتابوا فتاب الله عليهم.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Lote Tree marks the endpoint for those of Muhammad’s community who follow his way; its rivers, immense shade, and leaf covering the community are described, and God speaks to the Prophet there.
rows.anchor: هذه السدرة ينتهي إليها كل أحد خلا من أمتك على سنتك. فإذا هي شجرة يخرج من أصلها أنهار من ماء غير آسن،

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: At the Tree the Prophet lists favors given to earlier prophets, then God says He also chose him as friend, sent him universally, opened his breast, lifted his mention, and made his community the best, middle, first, and last.
rows.anchor: وقد اتخذتك خليلا -وهو مكتوب في التوراة: حبيب الرحمن (3) -وأرسلتك إلى الناس كافة بشيرا ونذيرا، وشرحت لك صدرك،

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: God grants the Prophet the seven oft-repeated verses, the closing verses of al-Baqara, al-Kawthar, eight religious privileges, and the role of opener and seal.
rows.anchor: وأعطيتك سبعا من المثاني لم يعطها نبي قبلك، وأعطيتك خواتيم سورة البقرة من كنز تحت العرش لم أعطها نبيا قبلك،

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: The Prophet names six further distinctions: opening and closing eloquence, universal mission, awe cast into enemies from a month’s distance, lawful spoils, and the whole earth as a place of purification and prayer.
rows.anchor: فضلني ربي بست: أعطاني فواتح الكلام (4) وخواتيمه وجوامع الحديث، وأرسلني إلى الناس كافة بشيرا ونذيرا

rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: Moses repeatedly tells the Prophet to seek fewer than fifty prayers because his community is weaker than Israel; reductions proceed by tens until five remain, with each counting as ten.
rows.anchor: فإن أمتك أضعف الأمم، فقد لقيت من بني إسرائيل شدة، قال: فرجع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى ربه،

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: The Prophet declines to ask again after the reduction to five, accepting the remaining obligation; Moses is described as most insistent at the start and most helpful on the return.
rows.anchor: قد رجعت إلى ربي حتى استحييت، فما أنا براجع إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī version is suspect because its narrator’s memory was poor; its strange material may combine several reports or describe another dream rather than the Israʾ.
rows.anchor: الأظهر أنه سيئ الحفظ ففيما تفرد به نظر. وهذا الحديث في بعض ألفاظه غرابة ونكارة شديدة،

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A sound report in al-Bukhārī and Muslim describes Moses as wiry-haired, Jesus as medium-height and ruddy, and Abraham as the Prophet’s closest physical likeness among his descendants.
rows.anchor: مضطرب، رجل الرأس، كأنه من رجال شنوءة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet chooses milk rather than wine and is told that he chose the natural disposition; had he taken wine, his community would have strayed.
rows.anchor: فأخذت اللبن، فشربت، فقيل لي: هديت الفطرة -أو: أصبت الفطرة-أما إنك لو أخذت الخمر غوت أمتك
